source.title: Spatial Colour Mixing Illusions as a Perception Stress Test for Vision-Language Models
source.authors: Nicoleta Basoc; Adrian Cosma; Emilian Radoi

record.tranche_reason: Tests downstream task accuracy across model scales, using visual-task accuracy rather than pretraining loss and in a structured-distortion setting.
record.gate_note: The study tests whether increasing language-model scale reliably improves VLM task performance under spatial colour distortions. It does not measure held-out cross-entropy, fit power laws, test extrapolation or compute-optimal allocations, or compare architecture shapes at fixed parameter count. Preprocessing and tool-use results are not rows for the scale claim; encoder-similarity results also do not measure the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study compares downstream accuracy of three released sizes in each of three VLM families on distorted-image recognition. It reports that language-model scale does not reliably improve accuracy, which bears on V6 in a new out-of-distribution setting. It fits no laws and measures no loss, so V1–V5 and V7 are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Accuracy collapses even at low distortion, and increasing language-model scale does not reliably mitigate this. Model family and vision-encoder inductive bias matter more than scale. The authors also conclude that humans are far more robust, and that low-pass preprocessing recovers part of the performance while tool availability does not.
record.recipe_differences: Compares downstream visual-task accuracy across existing VLM sizes under image distortions, rather than measuring language-model pretraining loss or fitting scaling laws.
record.method_sensitivity: Model family matters more than language-model scale in the reported comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: Within each encoder family (SigLIP, DINOv3), larger encoders give similar cosine similarity between clean and distorted embeddings; training objective matters more than encoder scale (Fig. 8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Vision-encoder scale has little effect on representational robustness to structured colour distortions.

record.problems: The text gives qualitative scale trends rather than exact scale-specific accuracy values. The compared models differ by family and may differ in visual encoders and other design choices, so the scale comparison is not an isolated controlled scaling experiment.
record.rows_left_out: No other scale-related results were reported as separate numerical or explicit scale comparisons. Preprocessing, tool-use, human-comparison, and encoder-similarity findings were left out because they do not test V6's scale-predictability relation.

untested.parts: Predictability from pretraining loss; any fitted trend; in-distribution downstream tasks (undistorted accuracy is near ceiling for all sizes); vision-encoder scaling of task accuracy.

missing.what: On MME, the largest models (Qwen3-VL-30B, gemma3-27b) collapse to nonsensical or off-task outputs on some illusion types. This is a possible case where larger models do worse, relevant to V6 direction.
Per-scale accuracy curves by dataset and illusion, needed to tell absent from partial scale effects for LLaVA and Qwen3-VL.

record.verdict_notes: This is weak evidence for V6: three sizes per family, released models with differing training recipes, and qualitative statements only. The limits_scope label applies to robustness under out-of-distribution structured distortions, not to downstream scaling in general.

versions.untested_parts: Pretraining-loss predictability and downstream performance outside the tested VLM tasks and spatial-distortion settings.

rows.subject: Nine VLMs across Gemma3, LLaVA, and Qwen3-VL families (scale comparison)
rows.size_stated: Three scales per family: Gemma3 4B, 12B, 27B; LLaVA 7B, 13B, 34B; Qwen3-VL 4B, 8B, 30B
rows.operation_detail: Compared task accuracy across model scales under spatial colour mixing distortions.

conditions.value: Eight spatial colour mixing variants at varying degrees

rows.value: The study states that increasing language-model scale does not reliably mitigate the failure; differences are driven more by model family than by language-model scale.
rows.note: Reported as an across-model and across-dataset trend; exact scale-specific accuracy values are presented in Figure 4 but are not stated in the text.
rows.check: The state rests on the authors' qualitative statement only; Figure 4 values cannot be read from the text. The scale comparison is confounded: LLaVA-34B is v1.6 while the 7B/13B are v1.5, and Qwen3-VL uses a larger encoder for larger models. These are released models, not a controlled scaling series.

rows.subject: Gemma3 models (4B, 12B, and 27B)
rows.operation_detail: Compared task accuracy across the three Gemma3 model scales.

conditions.value: Across the evaluated datasets and illusion types

rows.value: Performance across scales is described as almost identical.
rows.note: Family-level trend stated by the authors; no numeric scale-specific values are given in the text.
rows.check: Text says Gemma3 accuracy across scales is 'almost identical'. Gemma3 shares a frozen 400M SigLIP encoder across sizes, so this is the cleanest language-model-scale comparison in the study. Exact values are not given in the text.

relationships.condition: Off-the-shelf VLMs (Gemma3 4B–27B, LLaVA 7B–34B, Qwen3-VL 4B–30B) on object, artist and landmark recognition and MME under spatial colour mixing distortions
relationships.reason: Authors state language-model scale does not reliably improve accuracy; Gemma3 sizes perform almost identically and model family dominates (R1, R2). Evidence is qualitative and from uncontrolled released models.
relationships.display_finding: Gemma3 sizes performed almost identically and model family dominated accuracy differences in qualitative comparisons of released models.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: VLM task accuracy under the tested spatial colour mixing distortions
reader_labels.reason: The reported scale comparison does not show reliable accuracy gains, and Gemma3 performance is nearly identical across sizes; this limits predictable scale improvement in this setting (R1, R2).
